requirements.title: Core courses
requirements.summary: Complete all three core courses for 7.5 semester hours.

requirements.title: Approved electives
requirements.summary: Complete at least 7.5 semester hours from the published electives; the additional approved-electives section remains unresolved.

requirements.title: Eligibility and application
requirements.summary: Open to all Notre Dame majors, including Mendoza. The application opens once in the fall and once in the spring.

requirements.title: Major overlap and prerequisite conditions
requirements.summary: Up to three credits from major(s) may count toward the minor. Some elective prerequisites are outside the minor; consult an advisor.

requirements.title: Additional approved electives unresolved
requirements.summary: The additional approved electives across Notre Dame button shows no additional content after ordinary public-browser expansion on 2026-10-10; the full approved inventory remains unverified.

requirements.title: Minor total
requirements.summary: Complete 15 semester hours in the core and eligible electives.

requirements.title: University grading rule and college wording conflict
requirements.summary: University Code §3.3.11 excludes declared-program courses from the elective pass/fail option and bars pass/fail from satisfying program requirements. Mendoza’s BBA paragraph mentions an exception for the first course of a minor while also prohibiting business courses; applicability requires clarification.

requirements.title: Outside-course approval
requirements.summary: Before enrollment elsewhere, obtain dean/designee approval. Transfer requires C or better (not C-minus), standard letter grading, applicable nonduplicative content, and institutional/delivery review. Online courses require an appropriate synchronous component; the dean determines application to the credential.

requirements.title: Cross-college double counting
requirements.summary: For credentials across colleges, overlap requires both deans’ approval. The program’s three-hour major-overlap cap still applies.

requirements.title: Repeat limits
requirements.summary: Unless designated repeatable, only failed courses or approved D-grade courses may be repeated; credit counts once and both grades affect GPA. A D course may be repeated once, with two such repeats over the undergraduate career.

requirements.title: College completion constraint
requirements.summary: Mendoza students must complete added minors within four years. The BBA’s degree-wide GPA/residency requirements are not relabeled as minor-specific limits.

requirements.title: Mendoza pass-fail wording — applicability unresolved
requirements.summary: The BBA paragraph permits juniors/seniors one non-business elective per term with academic-adviser permission and assistant-dean approval, selected in the first six days and irrevocable. It excludes business/required/second-major/minor courses but parenthetically excepts a first minor-track course. This source-specific observation does not override the university code or grant an AI-minor exception, especially for students outside Mendoza.

requirements.title: Additional approved-elective section is empty
requirements.summary: The public additional-approved-electives accordion contains an empty content container. No finite additional pool or approval rule can be verified from this section; it is not evidence that no additional electives exist.

requirements.title: Arts and Letters home-college overlap — reconciliation needed
requirements.summary: For Arts and Letters students, the college describes replacing a shared program requirement with an approved course and retaining five unique minor courses/15 credits. University/college requirements may still overlap. The AI Essentials page separately allows three major credits to overlap; the public sources do not explain how that permission interacts with this college baseline. A joint approved exception is not inferred.

requirements.title: Arts and Letters home-college grading
requirements.summary: The Arts and Letters elective pass/fail option requires dean permission and junior/senior standing. It excludes courses in declared major, supplementary-major or minor disciplines and university/college core requirements. This is a home-college condition, not permission to use pass/fail in this minor.

requirements.title: Engineering students taking an outside-college credential
requirements.summary: Engineering explicitly limits its internal multi-counting rule to Engineering programs. An outside-college secondary credential follows its home college’s policies or an agreement between the colleges; questions go to the Associate Dean for Undergraduate Programs. Engineering’s internal unlimited overlap rule is not applied to this Mendoza minor.

requirements.title: Science home-college approval and completion
requirements.summary: Science expressly includes Mendoza minors among cross-college combinations. Program directors and the Science dean must formally accept the combination; substantial overlap prevents approval. Changes to a minor are generally expected not to extend study beyond eight semesters or require an overload.

requirements.title: Science home-college uniqueness and counting
requirements.summary: For Science students, a course may count once at each listed tier: university/core; college/primary major; and other programs, subject to the stated exception for a defined Science program. Each program must have at least 50% unique courses. This condition supplements the AI minor’s own overlap limit; it is not a new universal credit minimum.

notes: Published total is 15 credit hours: 7.5 core plus at least 7.5 elective hours. FIN 40260 / 40262 is preserved as one grouped listing, not two separately required courses. The empty additional-electives section prevents complete inventory certification.
Course theme categories are editorial classifications; source-stated outcomes are labeled separately. Unknown prerequisite values do not mean there are no prerequisites.

Academic Code §5.4.2 explicitly identifies all course credits as semester hours; numeric amounts are unchanged. The public additional-electives button was expanded and remained empty, so no hidden approved list is guessed.

The university prohibits pass/fail coursework from satisfying program requirements; the college lists a first-minor-course exception in its BBA policy. Its applicability to this all-majors minor remains unresolved. No degree-wide residency percentage or GPA is imposed as a minor-specific rule.

2026-10-11 reinspection confirms the unresolved source wording/list issue. Secondary parsers now observe the current catalog pool and pass-fail paragraph independently; blank catalog hours do not overwrite reviewed course amounts. No source-precedence rule authorizing a merged pool or grading exception was found in these sections.
